exams.syllabus: ABRSM Woodwind Practical Grades from 2026 (the 2022 lists may still be used until 31 December 2026). Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: 150 total: three pieces 30 each (90), scales and arpeggios 21, sight-reading 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in every component is not required). UK UCAS points for G6-8 (Pass/Merit/Distinction): G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30.

Three pieces, one from each of List A (faster, agile), List B (lyrical, expressive) and List C (varied styles/traditions); the repertoire lists are the same as for Performance Grades. Live piano accompaniment required unless the piece is a solo/study; recorded accompaniment not allowed. At G1-3 some or all pieces may use woodwind accompaniment: DUET pieces (play upper part), DUET/PIANO either. Up to two unaccompanied SOLO pieces may be played. Some grades (e.g. Descant G2, G4; Flute G2, G3, G4, G6, G8; Oboe G1, G4, G6, G8; Clarinet G7; Bassoon G3; Sax G1, G2, G4) require at least one accompanied piece. Listed arrangement/transcription editions must be used; otherwise any edition. Repeats generally not played except short ones; da capo/dal segno followed; cadenzas omitted. May play from memory (examiner needs a copy). Related-instrument options: Descant may play one piece on tenor or treble recorder (then A/B/C lists still apply); Treble G1-5 may play one piece on descant, G6-8 on another recorder where indicated; Saxophones may play one piece (any list) on another saxophone; Flute G8 one piece on alto flute and Oboe G8 one on cor anglais where indicated. Pieces from the 2022 syllabus allowed until 31 Dec 2026 (all requirements from the same syllabus).

Practical Grades are face-to-face exams; ABRSM also offers Performance Grades (separate qualifications focusing on a whole performance) using the same repertoire lists, and digital exams; marks cannot be transferred between Practical and Performance Grades, and using different pieces for both is recommended. Alternative tests exist for specific needs (blind/partially sighted: Braille memory or aural repetition for sight-reading; deaf/hearing-impaired: alternative aural tests).

DESCANT recorder: Scales: C, F maj; D min (nat/harm/mel, candidate's choice) - 1 oct | Arpeggios: C, F maj; D min - 1 oct | Articulation: tongued/slurred (examiner's choice)  ||  TREBLE recorder: Scales: F, B♭ maj; G min (nat/harm/mel) - 1 oct | Arpeggios: F, B♭ maj; G min - 1 oct | Articulation: tongued/slurred (examiner's choice)

Descant keys (majors; minors) C, F / Treble keys F, B♭. 4 bars; 4/4, 3/4; dotted minims to paired quavers and rests; tongued notes or simple two-note slurs; dynamics (recorders mf only; others f and mf)

Unseen extract ~2 grades lower, 30 s preparation; range a 5th; keys (cumulative): G major (descant).

Music published with an accompaniment must be performed with one; any suitable instrument may accompany provided the candidate stays the main soloist, candidates arrange their own accompanist, and pre-recorded accompaniments are not allowed unless the composer intended them. Memory is not required (but encouraged if it helps). Any edition matching the list entry may be used and own-choice music must exist as a legible, fully notated score; performing from unauthorised photocopies of copyright editions is not allowed. Own-choice may include the candidate's own composition or arrangement but must still be at or above the required standard, and ABRSM cannot give prior approval of own-choice standard. An audience is encouraged but not required. Infringements (wrong length, too much own choice without approval, wrong movements, edited video) can bring a warning, mark deduction or disqualification. A video can only ever be submitted once, and the same Unit 2 work cannot be reused at a higher level.

z00133.d: Siciliana and Spirituoso from Telemann's A minor sonata (Der getreue Musikmeister): a gently rocking slow movement then a lively second, training breath control, ornament and agility.

z00291.d: Duet pieces by Gale (Future Bright or Rico Town), easy contemporary educational recorder duets. Practises rhythm, listening and basic phrasing in ensemble.

z00292.d: Affetuoso and Presto Aria from Telemann's Eb recorder partita: a slow song then a fast dance. Practises ornament, agility and contrast.

z00293.d: Vivaldi's Cantabile from Il Gardellino, a gentle slow movement with floating line. Practises sustained tone and phrasing.

z00294.d: Aria 6: Tempo di Minuet from Telemann's G major partita for solo recorder, a graceful minuet. Practises steady rhythm and clean articulation.

z00295.d: Andante from Telemann's A minor sonata, a gentle flowing movement. Practises phrasing, breath planning and tuneful tone.

z00296.d: Siciliano from Bach's Eb flute sonata (BWV 1031) in recorder arrangement: gentle, lilting dotted rhythm. Practises expressive phrasing and ornament.

z00297.d: Choice of Handel's Allegro from the Sonata in Bb, HWV 377, or the gavotte-style finale of the Sonata in C, HWV 365: bright Baroque movements. Practises articulation and ornament.

z00298.d: Menuetts I and II from Telemann's F major recorder concerto, graceful contrasting dances. Practises light articulation and Baroque phrasing.

z00299.d: Grave and Allegro Aria from Telemann's G minor partita for solo recorder: serious opening and quick finale. Practises expressive contrast and agile fingerwork.

z00300.d: Larghetto and Andante from Handel's G minor recorder sonata: calm lyrical movements with Baroque ornament. Practises breath control and expression.

z00301.d: Vivaldi's Allegro finale of Il Gardellino, a bright, bird-like movement with fast passagework. Practises tonguing and fingerwork.

z00302.d: Handel's Adagio and Allegro for descant: a lyrical slow then brisk movement in G. Practises Baroque style and articulation.

z00303.d: Andante, Vivace and Presto Arias from Telemann's E minor partita for solo recorder. Practises contrasts, agility and phrase shape.

z00304.d: Ciaconna Allegro from Marcello's sonata in F: a lively dance over a ground bass. Practises articulation, rhythm and Baroque style.

z00305.d: Adagio and Allegro from Corelli's sonata with ornamented line: practises Baroque ornament, expressive adagio and brisk Allegro.

z00306.d: First and second movements of a Corelli violin sonata arranged for recorder, with ornamented line required. Practises ornament, phrasing and agility.

z00307.d: Slow expressive and witty fast movements from Hand's Sonatina No. 1, a modern work for recorder. Practises contemporary rhythms and contrast.

z00308.d: Andante and Vivace from Telemann's F minor sonata with repeats: expressive then brisk movements. Practises Baroque ornament and agility.

z00309.d: Vivaldi's Presto from La tempesta di mare: a very fast, stormy movement. Practises fast articulation, stamina and clean fingerwork.

z00310.d: Vivaldi's Allegro from the A minor concerto, fast and rhythmic. Practises articulation and agile fingerwork.

z00311.d: Bourrée Anglaise from Bach's A minor Partita for solo flute (BWV 1013), a jaunty unaccompanied dance. Practises articulation, rhythm and breath planning.

Machaut: French poet and composer, leading figure of the Ars Nova.
Notari: Italian singer and composer who worked in London.
Bononcini: Italian Baroque composer and cellist, who worked in Rome, Vienna and London.
Krähmer: Austrian oboist, composer and recorder player.
Beethoven: Towering composer who bridged the Classical and Romantic eras, transforming the symphony, sonata and string quartet.
Christopher Brown: English composer of church and instrumental music.
Merula: Italian early Baroque composer and organist.
Jean Baptiste Loeillet: Baroque composer from Ghent who published recorder and flute sonatas in Amsterdam.
Chevalier de Saint-Georges: Guadeloupe-born violinist, fencer and composer; a leading Parisian musician of his day.
Bigaglia: Venetian Baroque composer who wrote sonatas for recorder.
F. Mancini: Italian Baroque composer in Naples; wrote recorder sonatas.
Bricusse & Newley: English songwriting team behind hits including Pure Imagination.
John Wilson: British composer of light, pastoral oboe pieces.
Menken, arr. Lawrance: American composer of Disney film scores and musicals. Arranged/edited by Lawrance.
F. Couperin: Leading French Baroque composer and harpsichordist, known as 'le Grand', famous for his harpsichord ordres and chamber music.
V. Ellis & Grey: English songwriting team behind Spread a Little Happiness.
Joannes Collette: Composer of melodious studies for recorder.
Gillian Whitehead: New Zealand composer known for operas and chamber music.
Valentine: English recorder player and composer working in Italy.
Vivaldi: Venetian Baroque composer and violinist who wrote hundreds of concertos, including The Four Seasons.
Golland: English composer and teacher who wrote educational works.
Wei Weng Cheng: Contemporary composer of music for recorder.

Composer of the original aria Bist du bei mir, attributed to Bach in the Notebook.
Barsanti: Italian recorder, oboe and flute player who worked in London and Edinburgh, then Scotland.
Frescobaldi: Organist at St Peter's in Rome and the most influential keyboard composer of the early Baroque.
Praetorius, arr. Capek: German Renaissance composer, known for the Terpsichore dance collection. Arranged/edited by Capek.
J S Bach, arr. Nitz: German Baroque composer of the Brandenburg Concertos and Passions. Arranged/edited by Nitz.
Hedges: English composer and lecturer who wrote much accessible orchestral, choral and educational music.
Flinn: Contemporary composer; little reliable information held.
Leenhouts: Dutch recorder player and conductor, member of Amsterdam Loeki Stardust Quartet.
Quantz: Flautist and composer, teacher to Frederick the Great, author of a famous flute treatise.
